model_output.verdict: A computer science graduate with software projects and an internship that needs more detail.
write_up: Your resume points to Software Engineer roles: you have a Cardinal Health internship, a campus ordering app and Python projects. It's common for an early-career resume to lean on duties, but the internship lines don't yet show which features, tests or fixes were yours. That makes it tough to stand out in a pile.

The Personal Finance Tracker line is a good model: it names the application, what it does and the tools you used. Your education is useful, but you also have internship and help desk experience, so put Experience above Education.

Let's start with the Cardinal Health feature line, then make the tests and fixes concrete. Replace the generic objective with a short introduction grounded in your work, and use the space taken by soft skills for details about your projects or internship.

cards.line: Motivated and detail-oriented Computer Science graduate seeking a Software Engineer position where I can leverage my technical skills and passion for problem solving to contribute to a dynamic team.
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see the job you want, but not what makes your software work distinctive. The internship and projects give you stronger material than a list of traits.

cards.question: Which feature from your internship best represents your work?

cards.line: Education sits above Experience.
cards.cannot_tell: Your internship and help desk roles give a recruiter work to look at before coursework. Moving Experience up brings that work into view sooner.
cards.question: Can you move Experience above Education?

cards.line: - Responsible for developing features for an internal inventory management web application using React and Spring Boot
cards.cannot_tell: The application and tools are named, but the features aren't. A recruiter can't tell what you built for the inventory team.
cards.example: Developed [feature] for an internal inventory management web application using React and Spring Boot
cards.question: Which feature did you develop for the inventory application?

cards.line: - Participated in daily stand-ups and sprint planning meetings as part of an Agile team
cards.cannot_tell: Meeting participation alone doesn't show your contribution to the team's software work. Give the recruiter something you brought to planning or shipped with the team.
cards.example: Participated in daily stand-ups and sprint planning meetings as part of an Agile team, contributing [contribution]
cards.question: What did you contribute to planning or delivery with the team?

cards.line: - Wrote unit tests to improve code quality and reliability
cards.cannot_tell: Unit tests are useful work, but the recruiter can't tell what you tested. Name the feature or behavior the tests covered.
cards.example: Wrote unit tests for [feature or behavior] to improve code quality and reliability
cards.question: What feature or behavior did your unit tests cover?

cards.line: - Collaborated with cross-functional teams to gather requirements and deliver solutions
cards.cannot_tell: The teams and solutions are left unnamed, so your part in the work is difficult to picture. One example would make the collaboration concrete.
cards.example: Collaborated with [teams] to gather requirements and deliver [solution]
cards.question: Which teams did you work with, and what solution did you help deliver?

cards.line: - Fixed bugs and performed code reviews
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can't tell what kind of bugs you fixed or what code you reviewed. An example of each would show the work behind the tasks.
cards.example: Fixed [bug] and performed code reviews for [code or feature]
cards.question: What bug did you fix, and what code or feature did you review?

cards.line: - Resolved tickets in a timely manner and documented solutions
cards.cannot_tell: The line doesn't show how many tickets you handled or what kind of solution you documented. Either detail would give the support work more substance.
cards.example: Resolved [number] tickets [frequency] and documented solutions for [issue]
cards.question: How many tickets did you handle in a typical period, and what is one issue you documented?

cards.line: - Built a Python application to track expenses and visualize spending with matplotlib
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It tells a recruiter what you made and what someone can use it for, with the relevant tools attached.

fit.why: Your objective names Software Engineer, and your internship and projects show application development.
fit.level: entry level, a software engineering internship and a recent computer science degree
fit.note: Your React and Spring Boot internship and full-stack capstone give you material for entry-level software roles. Put the features you personally built at the center of that story.
